newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on S.Africa fallout.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on S.Africa fallout.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Thursday, reflecting concern over South Africa's shock overnight announcement that it would switch diplomatic ties to Beijing from Taipei in 1997, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 0.82 percent or 56.55 points lower at 6,876.41. Turnover was a strong T$82.26 billion.

President Nelson Mandela's announcement, made on Wednesday long after the Taiwan market close, fuelled concern about big Taiwan investments in South Africa and about Taiwan's economic outlook under arch rival China's long shadow. The decision will strip Taiwan of the biggest of its 30 diplomatic allies.
Brokers were quick to note that Taiwan's market was ripe for profit-taking even without such a jarring political jolt.

"The market was encountering serious resistance after rising so much in the past two weeks, so many blue-chips fell off today in a normal correction," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
Before Thursday the index had gained nearly 400 points since November 15 in a dramatic show of investor optimism.
The fundamentals-backed electronic sector, which had led the recent bull run, dropped 2.09 percent with Rectron plunging the daily seven percent limit or T$1.20 to T$16.30.
Acer Inc, Taiwan's largest computer firm, lost T$1.50 to close at T$53 with the session's single heaviest trade volume of 88.07 million shares.
There were no signs of panic selling despite the political blow of Taipei losing its biggest diplomatic ally.
"Many investors knew it (the severing of ties) was coming, and they felt it would not have a significant effect on the economy," said Yungli Securities analyst Chen Han-chung.
Financials sustained the least damage as government-backed funds were seen buying major bank shares to prevent the overall index from plunging on the diplomatic loss, brokers said.
